newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares edge up, seen falling on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares edge up, seen falling on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares edged up in slightly lower turnover on Friday, extending last two sessions' gains but analysts said stronger selling after price fixing signalled a fall on Monday.
"I suspect we will have falls at the beginning of the week but later the WIG is likely to stabilise at between 13,500 and 14,000 points," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.1 percent, to 13,706.3, and turnover fell 5.7 percent to 91 million zlotys ($31.4 million) on both markets as 35 issues rose, 29 fell and 19 were flat.
Analysts said, however, the bourse was likely to stay locked in the already six-week long sideways drift next week, with no signals to push the market off either way.

They expected some stocks to jump or fall in speculation before the release of companies' monthly earnings for November, most of them due on Wednesday, but said the individual stock swings were unlikely to affect the WIG index moves.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 9.9 million zlotys ($3.4 million) with four stocks falling, one rising and four staying flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 4.2 percent in 46-million-zloty ($15.9 million) continuous trade and fell 2.7 percent in a 28.5-million-zloty ($9.8 million) turnover in regular session.
